parsed_review.motivation: The code change introduces support for OpenAI Text-to-Speech (TTS) capabilities within the Spring AI framework using the official OpenAI Java SDK. This enables developers to easily configure and utilize audio speech generation features through standard Spring Boot auto-configuration and property-based settings.
parsed_review.good_points:
Correct use of @ConfigurationProperties for managing model configuration in a Spring-idiomatic way.
Comprehensive suite of integration and unit tests covering default and custom configurations.
Proper resource management for input streams using try-with-resources to prevent memory leaks.
Clean abstraction of rate limit metadata using HTTP header extraction.
Correct implementation of the AutoConfiguration setup and dependency injection pattern.
parsed_review.bad_points:
The code uses a raw RuntimeException when handling IO errors in the model execution.
The logger naming convention triggered a static analysis warning, although it currently follows standard Java conventions; the PMD warning might be a false positive related to the specific ruleset configuration.
Tight coupling between the model implementation and the underlying HTTP client setup logic.
parsed_review.suggestion: Define a specific domain exception (e.g., OpenAiSdkAudioException) to wrap checked IOExceptions instead of throwing raw RuntimeException. Additionally, consider decoupling the OpenAI client creation process further by abstracting the client factory logic, though the current builder pattern is acceptable for the project scale.
parsed_review.implementation_details:
OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechAutoConfiguration.java: Registers the OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel bean. Uses OpenAiSdkAutoConfigurationUtil to resolve properties. Configures the OpenAI client via OpenAiSdkSetup.
OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel.java: Implements the TextToSpeechModel interface. Uses a builder pattern for configuration and client injection. Handles the conversion of HTTP responses to speech bytes. Implements a non-streaming approach to meet current SDK limitations.
OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechResponseMetadata.java: Parses OpenAI specific rate-limit headers into a standardized format.

issues.title: Use of Raw RuntimeException
issues.detail: The call method in OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel throws a raw RuntimeException when an IOException occurs. This is not ideal for error handling; a more specific custom exception should be used.

issues.title: Potential Naming Convention Violation
issues.detail: Static analysis flagged the logger field name 'logger' as a potential violation of constant naming rules, although this usually pertains to static final variables meant as constants rather than loggers.

interpretation_references: Implement text-to-speech functionality using the OpenAI Java SDK (v4.17.0).
Add OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel, a TextToSpeechModel implementation using the OpenAI Java SDK and OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechOptions.
Add OpenAiSdkRateLimit which can be retrieved from the Audio speech model HttpResponse headers.
interpretation_candidates: Introduced support for OpenAI Audio Speech using the official OpenAI Java SDK by adding OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechModel, OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechOptions, and their corresponding auto-configuration (OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechAutoConfiguration) and property classes.
Added necessary metadata handling for rate limits via OpenAiSdkAudioSpeechResponseMetadata and created corresponding integration and unit tests.
The current Spring AI OpenAI implementation relies on direct REST/WebClient calls.
The project is migrating towards utilizing the official OpenAI Java SDK for better maintenance, stability, and access to new features.

This change provides the necessary infrastructure to use the official SDK for text-to-speech functionality, enabling users to choose between the legacy REST-based implementation and the new SDK-based one via configuration properties.
